requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 communicate through node1 (private links must be configured to actually route through node1)
requirements.summary: node1 eth1/eth2 and node2/node3 enp8s0 were unconfigured; executor assigned static IPs and specific routes and confirmed ttl=63 pings between node2 and node3, proving traffic transits node1 as a 3-hop path.

requirements.requirement: Limit traffic from node2 toward node3 to 1 Mbit/s
requirements.summary: A VyOS qos shaper policy (bandwidth/ceiling 1mbit) was applied as an egress policy on node1 eth2 (the node3-facing link). tc showed htb qdisc active, and iperf3 measured throughput dropping from a ~20 Gbps unshaped baseline to ~0.84-0.92 Mbit/s after shaping, both immediately and after all three nodes were rebooted.

requirements.requirement: Leave traffic from node3 toward node2 unrestricted
requirements.summary: No shaper was applied to eth1 (node2-facing link). iperf3 measured ~19.1 Gbps baseline and ~1.5 Gbps post-shaping (limited only by iperf3/CPU, not by any tc policy) node3->node2, confirming the reverse direction remains unrestricted.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task were directly and coherently demonstrated: the previously-unconfigured private links were established so node2/node3 route through node1, a VyOS htb qos shaper was applied to the node3-facing egress link limiting node2->node3 to ~0.84-0.92 Mbit/s (down from a ~20 Gbps baseline), and node3->node2 remained unrestricted (~1.5 Gbps) throughout. The executor additionally ran the provider-wide restart evidence protocol on all three nodes with clear pre-restart boot-identity/healthy-state capture, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state (including a re-verified 1 Mbit/s cap after all three nodes were rebooted), well beyond what the public task contract required, and cross-checked cleanly against the fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots. Minor hygiene residue (uncleaned test-result JSON and log files in /tmp on node2/node3) is the only notable imperfection.
limitations: Restart/reboot was not part of the public task's material contract, so its evidence quality affects confidence and hygiene framing only, not the satisfied status of the three shaping/topology requirements.
Small residual temp files (iperf3 result JSON, iperf_server.log, reboot.log) were left on node2 and node3 after testing; low-risk but not cleaned up.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 67 executor commands chronologically. State-changing actions (static IP/route assignment on all three nodes, VyOS qos policy commit/save, iperf3 package installs, temporary firewalld port openings for testing) all had a clear role in establishing the topology, applying the shaper, or collecting bounded throughput evidence. Firewalld ports opened for iperf3 testing were reliably closed afterward (cmd-93acfeae24a047f9, cmd-ac126dcfa7da4b6f, cmd-6eb9dd26635647a0, cmd-6ad71c1a56f14991), and iperf3 server processes were killed after each test. However, several diagnostic/result files were left behind on node2 and node3 (/tmp/res.json, /tmp/res_shaped.json, /tmp/res_post_reboot.json, /tmp/res_final.json, /tmp/iperf_server.log, /tmp/reboot.log on node2; /tmp/res_rev.json, /tmp/res_rev_shaped.json, /tmp/iperf_server.log, /tmp/reboot.log on node3), visible in the after_executor snapshot as residue not present at before_prepare. These are low-risk, non-destructive artifacts but constitute unnecessary/uncleaned mutation. A handful of command failures (VyOS 'show'/'run' syntax not available in bash context, an initial dnf GPG-key parsing failure on node2, and python JSON KeyErrors before the iperf3 server was reachable) were read-only or self-corrected diagnostic issues with no lasting negative effect.
